question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the passage overall? In vertical gene transfer, genetic material passes from a parent down to its offspring; horizontal gene transfer, by contrast, refers to genetic material being swapped between organisms that are not parent and offspring. Horizontal gene transfer occurs frequently in prokaryotes—single-celled organisms like the bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis and Lactobacillus curvatus—but it has seldom been documented in eukaryotes (multicellular organisms). Recent research, though, indicates that horizontal gene transfer takes place among eukaryotes more often than scientists once believed.
option a: It argues that two biological phenomena are more similar than they may initially appear to be.
option b: It indicates a distinction between the mechanics of two kinds of biological processes.
option c: It contrasts the frequency with which a biological phenomenon has been detected in two categories of organisms.
option d: It explains why a common perception of a biological process is flawed.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence sets the rarity of the process in eukaryotes against its commonness in prokaryotes, contrasting how often it appears in two organism categories.

question: Based on the two texts, under which condition would the author of Text 2 be most likely to accept the forecasts presented in Text 1? Text 1: A conservation organization speaking for 11 tribal nations in the Great Lakes area conducted a study finding that, should temperatures climb as much as certain models predict, the region's walleye (ogaa in Ojibwe) will fare considerably worse over the coming half century. The black bear (makwa in Ojibwe), on the other hand, is expected to endure even the greatest projected warming with little harm. Text 2: Scientists need to exercise caution in forecasting how plants and animals will react to environmental changes ahead. Because ecosystems are intricate, broad generalizations are hard to make. It is a mistake to presume that any given species will behave identically in every location and era. Forecasts made without careful regard for local conditions tend to be wrong.
option a: The walleye and black bear in the Great Lakes are predicted to respond differently if temperatures rise only moderately than if temperatures rise to the highest predicted levels.
option b: The responses of the walleye and black bear predicted by this study are similar to the responses predicted by studies of other species from the Great Lakes.
option c: The predictions about the responses of the walleye and black bear are based on a thorough study of conditions in the Great Lakes specifically.
option d: Conditions in the Great Lakes are similar to conditions in other ecosystems where the walleye and black bear are predicted to experience increased temperatures.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Text 2 trusts forecasts grounded in local circumstances, so it would accept Text 1's predictions if they rested on a thorough study of the Great Lakes specifically.

question: According to the text, which statement about El Museo del Barrio is best supported? Established in 1969, El Museo del Barrio presents the visual arts and cultures of Latin America and of Latino communities within the United States. Based in New York City, it holds a collection of more than 8,500 objects. Since 2000, several additional institutions focused on Latino cultures have opened across the country. One prominent example is LA Plaza de Cultura y Artes in Los Angeles, which concentrates on Mexican American art and culture.
option a: It was founded after 2000.
option b: Its collection includes over 8,500 objects.
option c: It is no longer located in New York City.
option d: It is visited by more people than any other Latino cultural institution in the US.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text directly states the museum holds more than 8,500 objects.

question: Which quotation from a student who has been to the museum best illustrates the underlined claim? The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, in Boston, Massachusetts, holds an enormous collection of artworks. The museum has released digital images of many of its pieces, among them Dos Mujeres (Salvadora y Herminia) by Frida Kahlo and Supermodel by Kerry James Marshall. For some of these images, online viewers can zoom in extremely close. As a result, online viewers can examine certain artworks in greater detail than people viewing them inside the museum can.
option a: "I had heard about the painting by Frida Kahlo before, so I was excited to see it in the museum when I visited."
option b: "I visited the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, recently. Later, I remembered Supermodel and wanted to learn more about the artist."
option c: "I zoomed in on Dos Mujeres (Salvadora y Herminia) on my computer. I saw fine lines that I hadn't been able to see when I looked at the piece in the museum."
option d: "The first time I ever saw any art by Kerry James Marshall was when I went to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, with my class."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only the zoom quotation shows a viewer seeing more detail online than in the museum.

question: Which finding about Charadriiformes and the 12 other orders identified in the recent study, if true, would best support the researchers' prediction? When a predator approaches the nest of a pied oystercatcher (Haematopus longirostris), the bird draws the predator away from the nest by feigning an injury that leaves it unable to fly. Known as the "broken-wing display," this behavior was for a long time believed to occur only within the order Charadriiformes (shorebirds). Recent studies, however, have found that species belonging to Anseriformes (waterfowl), Cuculiformes (cuckoos), and 10 other bird orders also perform the display—especially those subject to high rates of predation. Because species facing higher predation rates tend to have shorter incubation periods, some researchers have proposed that the defensive behavior is linked to comparatively brief incubation periods.
option a: Nearly 90% of species in the order Charadriiformes have been observed using broken-wing display to deter predators during an incubation period, while only 30% of species in the other 12 orders have been observed doing so.
option b: Across those orders, broken-wing display has been observed in approximately 80% of species with incubation periods under 20 days and approximately 58% of species with incubation periods over 30 days.
option c: The use of broken-wing display has been confirmed in 285 individual species from those orders, representing a range of incubation periods, from a minimum of 10 days to a maximum of 44 days.
option d: The mean incubation period is 22 days for species from those orders, regardless of the species' use of broken-wing display.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A higher proportion of short-incubation species performing the display than long-incubation species supports the predicted link with brief incubation periods.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Numerous studies have identified a positive relationship between concentrations of dissolved organic carbon and mercury in freshwater bodies untouched by human activity. However, when Enelton Fagnani, José Roberto Guimarã, and Pedro Sérgio Fadini examined freshwater bodies affected by industrial activity, they found no such correlation, prompting some scientists to propose that the relationship might be unique to undisturbed waters. Yet Jeffrey D. Jeremiason and colleagues studied freshwater bodies disturbed by mining and obtained results resembling those from the undisturbed-water studies, which suggests that ______
option a: the effects of industrial activity on the association between levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury should not be taken as indicative of the effects of every type of human disturbance.
option b: disturbances linked to industrial activity affect significantly more bodies of fresh water than disturbances linked to mining do.
option c: Fagnani, Guimarã, and Fadini's study used different methods to measure the concentration of mercury in fresh water than Jeremiason and colleagues' study did.
option d: levels of dissolved organic carbon and mercury are both much higher in bodies of fresh water disturbed by industrial activity than they are in bodies of fresh water disturbed by mining.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Mining-disturbed waters showing the correlation implies industrial effects don't represent all human disturbances.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it follows the conventions of Standard English? In Los Angeles, the soprano and philanthropist Ellen Beach Yaw received an honor when Lark Ellen Avenue was named ______ her.
option a: after,
option b: after;
option c: after:
option d: after
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between the preposition "after" and its object "her."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it follows the conventions of Standard English? An element's atomic structure ______ where that element falls on the periodic table.
option a: determining
option b: to determine
option c: having determined
option d: determines
subject: Reading and Writing

question: Which choice completes the text so that it follows the conventions of Standard English? Numerous works by the Roman poet Lucan (1st century CE) are ______ his Pharsalia, an epic poem centered on Julius Caesar, survives as an extant work: it can still be read.
option a: lost, and conversely
option b: lost, conversely,
option c: lost and conversely,
option d: lost. Conversely,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period separates the two independent clauses, with the transition beginning the second sentence.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it follows the conventions of Standard English? Plant defense mechanisms fall into three primary categories: physical barriers, chemical defenses, and protein defenses. The English oak relies on a ______ these trees generate chemicals that interfere with the ability of certain plant-eating insects to digest their food.
option a: chemical defense
option b: chemical defense,
option c: chemical defense and
option d: chemical defense:
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon fits, introducing the explanation of what the chemical defense involves.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The San Lorenzo archaeological site sits in our home state of Veracruz, Mexico. ______ the ancient Olmec civilization left behind a 20-ton stone statue of a human head. In neighboring Tabasco stood another stone statue, this one weighing 24 tons.
option a: Therefore,
option b: Similarly,
option c: Here,
option d: In other words,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Here" points back to the San Lorenzo site just named as the location of the statue.

question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two sculptures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken these notes: The End, a 2010 sculpture by the Korean artist Jung Lee, is made of blue neon lighting that spells out its title phrase ("the end"). Pyramid (Yellow), a 2011 sculpture by the Mexican-Swiss artist Ana Roldán, is made of yellow neon lighting arranged into an abstract triangle shape.
option a: The neon lighting in The End is blue, but the lighting in Pyramid (Yellow) is yellow.
option b: Roldán's sculpture Pyramid (Yellow) consists of yellow neon lighting in an abstract triangle shape.
option c: Both Lee's and Roldán's sculptures are crafted from neon lighting.
option d: Rather than spelling out a phrase, Roldán's sculpture forms an abstract triangle shape.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice C names a feature the two sculptures share—both are made of neon lighting.

question: The student wants to indicate the location of the Isthmus of Avalon. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken these notes: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land, also called a land bridge, that joins two larger landmasses across a body of water. The Isthmus of Avalon links the Avalon Peninsula to Newfoundland. The Isthmus of Avalon is situated in Canada.
option a: An isthmus, or land bridge, like the Isthmus of Avalon, connects two larger pieces of land.
option b: The Isthmus of Avalon is located in Canada, where it connects the Avalon Peninsula to Newfoundland.
option c: An isthmus, also known as a land bridge, is a strip of land that connects two larger pieces of land across an expanse of water.
option d: One example of an isthmus is the Isthmus of Avalon.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B states where the isthmus is located—in Canada.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In Peru, young Quechua and Aymara musicians are ______ a new musical genre. Cay Sur and Renata Flores are two Indigenous artists shaping this new sound; they rap in Quechua and merge hip-hop beats with traditional Andean instruments and themes.
option a: repeating
option b: remembering
option c: developing
option d: correcting
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Developing" fits the artists creating a brand-new genre.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Bing Xie and her colleagues have found that plains zebras produce at least four kinds of vocalizations: "snorts," "soft snorts," "squeals," and "quagga quagga" calls. Using machine-learning algorithms to ______ the recorded sounds by type, the team discovered that snorts differ from one zebra to another, whereas squeals stay more consistent across zebra populations.
option a: categorize
option b: suppress
option c: extend
option d: collapse
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Categorize" fits sorting the recorded vocalizations according to type.

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? Ruth Asawa was a versatile artist who explored many forms, including her distinctive tied-wire sculptures, but her commitment extended well beyond making art. Asawa also sought to bring art to children in her hometown of San Francisco, California. Toward that end, she cofounded the Alvarado School Arts Workshop in 1968, which introduced artworks and artists into public schools, and in 1982 she helped establish a public arts high school in San Francisco that was later named in her honor.
option a: Asawa left a promising career as a sculptor to work as an art teacher in San Francisco schools.
option b: Asawa inspired many other artists to share their work with students in public schools.
option c: Asawa's unique sculptures were appreciated more by local art communities than they were nationwide.
option d: Asawa's interest in art education prompted her to create art programs for students in San Francisco.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage centers on how Asawa's commitment to art education led her to found programs for San Francisco students.

question: Which quotation from a translation of The Underdogs most effectively illustrates the claim? The Underdogs, a 1915 novel originally written in Spanish by Mariano Azuela, uses imagery drawn from nature to convey the mental state of its protagonist, Demetrio: ______
option a: "Demetrio laid a hand on his hair which covered his ears, and stretching himself out for a long time, seemed to be lost in thought."
option b: "Demetrio suppressed a sigh. Memories crowded and buzzed through his brain like bees about a hive."
option c: "Yet he was previous; an hour or more elapsed with no sound or stir save the song of the locust in the brush or the frog stirring in his mudhole."
option d: "At this hour, as usual, the calcinated rocks, the sun-burnt branches, and the dry weeds faded into the semi-obscurity of the shadows."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The simile comparing his memories to bees about a hive uses natural imagery to depict his mental state.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? The rise of online streaming has prompted many listeners to move away from owning music—whether through downloads or physical formats like compact discs—and toward streaming services such as YouTube Music and Jango. Datta et al. investigated how this shift affects the diversity of music that people listen to. The researchers noted that the ownership model attaches a cost to each song a listener acquires, so building variety is expensive, whereas streaming services generally charge a single flat fee for an entire catalog, making variety essentially free. This reasoning suggests that ______
option a: music publishers who choose to forgo releasing music on physical media are likely to see no change in revenue.
option b: listeners who prefer to purchase compact discs rather than use a service such as YouTube Music or Jango would tend to listen to older music.
option c: the music choices of listeners who use streaming services would likely be more varied than those of listeners who do not use streaming services.
option d: listeners who use streaming services would be more likely to give physical copies of music as gifts to others than to purchase physical copies for themselves.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If streaming makes variety free, streaming listeners should consume more varied music than non-streaming listeners.

option a: after;
option b: after:
option c: after,

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Plants called metal hyperaccumulators can aid in clearing heavy metal pollutants from soil. Paspalum fasciculatum, also known as bamboo grass, for example, can take up large amounts of cadmium and store it safely in its roots and shoots. ______ the plant's roots might not extend deep enough into the soil to remove the pollutant completely.
option a: On the contrary,
option b: For this reason,
option c: Moreover,
option d: Still,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Still" signals the contrast between the plant's usefulness and its limitation.
